metadata.description: The Forest Rights Act (FRA) of 2006 is a landmark legislation aimed at recognizing the traditional rights of forest-dwelling communities, including Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), over forests and their resources. Among its provisions is the recognition of Habitat Rights, which are critical for PVTGs, as these groups have unique socio-cultural and livelihood practices closely tied to their traditional habitats. By ensuring Habitat Rights, India can take a step closer to protecting its most vulnerable communities and upholding the spirit of the Forest Rights Act, which is rooted in justice, equity, and sustainability.
